name: AI Deep Dive — SPCX — 2026-06-13
rationale: SpaceX (SPCX) is a pre-IPO 3-segment aerospace and connectivity company trading on secondary markets. The core thesis is that Starlink's LEO broadband network — already at 49% gross margins and millions of subscribers — combined with a near-monopoly in orbital launch services creates a durable, compounding revenue stream. The current -26% net margin reflects Starship development capex, not underlying unit economics. As Starship commercializes and Starlink penetrates global markets, margins should expand significantly toward 15-22% over 5 years. The secondary market price of $160.95 represents 27% upside to a DCF-derived fair value of $204 at a 12% discount rate. Primary risks are Starship timeline execution, private market illiquidity, and a valuation that prices in meaningful growth expectations. UPDATE 2026-06-19: IPO completed 2026-06-12 at ~$185. Public float implies 7.57B total shares vs the 1.16B used in original DCF. Restated per-share FV is approximately $31 — current price is ~6x the restated DCF value. SELL.

bear.rationale: Starlink growth decelerates to 15% CAGR as Amazon Kuiper achieves commercial scale (2027-2028), eroding pricing power. FAA regulatory friction delays Starship commercial operations beyond 2029, meaning SpaceX continues burning $14B+/yr capex with limited near-term offset. Net margins recover only to 5% as competitive pressure and continued capex weigh. Exit multiple of 20x reflects aerospace/defense median (18x) with modest premium for uniqueness. Quality multiplier 1.2 anchored to (1) Falcon 9 cost advantage via vertical integration — ~60-70% cheaper than ULA; (2) Starlink first-mover satellite density advantage with 7,000+ LEO satellites deployed. Both moats persist even in bear scenario.

base.rationale: Starlink scales to 20M+ active subscribers globally by 2029, reaching $25-30B in segment revenue. Falcon 9 cadence sustains 100+ missions/year; pricing power maintained as competition remains 3+ years behind. Starship achieves commercial cargo operations by 2027-2028, beginning to offset development costs. 22% CAGR represents natural deceleration from historical 34% 2yr CAGR as penetration deepens in mature markets. Net margin recovery to 15% as Starship capex rolls off and Starlink segment reaches high incremental margins. Exit P/E of 35x reflects hybrid platform/aerospace classification — anchored to Tech Platform median (28x) with premium justified by network effects and launch monopoly, within ±30% deviation rule. Quality multiplier 1.2 anchored to dual structural moats cited in bear rationale.

bull.rationale: Catalyst: Starlink achieves 50M+ subscribers driven by Direct-to-Cell partnerships with major mobile operators (confirmed FCC spectrum licenses) and rapid emerging markets penetration. Starship fully commercial by 2027 with reusability rates matching Falcon 9, collapsing launch costs and opening new markets (point-to-point Earth transit, lunar logistics). xAI/Grok achieves enterprise-scale revenue from Starlink infrastructure synergies. 30% CAGR is aggressive but grounded in Starlink TAM ($1T+ broadband) still in early penetration. Net margin 22% reflects Starlink's near-zero marginal cost structure at scale. Exit P/E of 50x reflects Tech Platform growth multiple (45x benchmark) with modest premium for the dual-business compounding dynamic. This is the scenario where SpaceX becomes a multi-trillion dollar enterprise — named catalyst: Direct-to-Cell with T-Mobile/Verizon at scale.

aiThesis.rationale: SpaceX holds a defensible near-monopoly in orbital launch services (Falcon 9 at ~90% US market share) and is scaling Starlink into what may become the world's largest broadband network by subscriber count. The investment thesis rests on two structural moats: (1) vertical integration in launch enabling 60-70% cost advantage over ULA/Blue Origin — not closeable in the next 5 years; (2) Starlink constellation density (7,000+ LEO satellites) providing latency advantages that newer entrants cannot match without years of deployment. Current -26% net margin reflects intentional Starship development capex at ~$14B/yr, not structural weakness — gross margins of 49.4% confirm exceptional unit economics. The DCF model (12% discount rate, 5yr horizon) yields $204 weighted fair value vs $160.95 secondary market price, a 27% discount. However, this analysis carries LOW CONFIDENCE (0.45/1.0) due to: no audited financials, no analyst coverage, ambiguous share count (1.16B used per standardize_metrics.py vs 7.49B shares_outstanding in yfinance), and significant secondary market illiquidity. Position sizing should be conservative. The key trigger to increase conviction would be a public IPO filing or direct access to audited S-1 financial data.
aiThesis.ipoNote: IPO: 2026-06-12 at ~$185. Public share count 7.57B vs secondary-market assumption of 1.16B diluted. Prior DCF FV of $204/share was per-secondary-market-share. Restated per public share: total equity FV $237B / 7.57B shares = $31/share. At $185 public price, market cap is $1.40T vs $237B modeled equity — ~6x overvalued vs DCF. 75x P/S ratio. Pass at current price. Revisit if price declines toward $30-40 range or after audited S-1 financials clarify true diluted share count.
